question: A train is travelling at a speed of 180 km/hr. Brakes are applied so as to produce a uniform acceleration of (- 1 m/s²). What will be the distance covered by the train before coming to rest?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1620 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The initial speed (**u**) of the train is given as **180 km/hr**.
 
• To convert the speed into meters per second (m/s):

 1 km/hr = 5/18 m/s, so

 **u = 180 × (5/18) = 50 m/s**.
 
• The final speed (**v**) of the train is **0 m/s** because the train comes to rest.
 
• The acceleration (**a**) is given as **-1 m/s²** (negative because it is deceleration).
 
• We use the equation of motion: **v² = u² + 2as**, where:

 - **v** is the final velocity,

 - **u** is the initial velocity,

 - **a** is acceleration, and<br /&
